name: Consumption contract and CI vertical-neutrality gate (P16 EP-387)
skipReason: A CI gate and a markdown document — no runtime route exists. Verified by tests/platform/neutralityGate.test.ts (20 assertions), which plants REAL violations in a scratch package and asserts the gate exits non-zero naming file:line, then removes them; plus assertions over docs/CONSUMPTION-CONTRACT.md and .github/workflows/neutrality-gate.yml.
description: Publishes the written consumption contract and implements the CI neutrality gate. Proves all four criteria. WHY IT IS MECHANICAL: ProjexCloud is one horizontal platform — the same sdk-sla serves healthcare, field service and logistics tenants — so the moment a vertical's vocabulary leaks into an SDK it stops being reusable in the others and the usual remedy is a fork, which is how a platform quietly becomes four codebases. A domain word in a variable name reads as helpful specificity in review rather than as coupling, so it is close to invisible until the second vertical arrives; machines notice it every time. AC1: the gate greps SDK source for vertical nouns, business stage names, role-name branches and hardcoded business rules, exiting 1 on any hit — tested by PLANTING each violation class in a scratch package and asserting the non-zero exit, i.e. by pulling the alarm rather than reading it. AC2: output leads with file:line, then the category and the offending text, and closes by telling the author what to do instead (resolver, config value, tenant-configurable rule) with a pointer to the contract — a gate that says only 'neutrality violated' gets suppressed because nobody can act on it. AC3: docs/CONSUMPTION-CONTRACT.md states the governing rule (an SDK owns a mechanism; an application owns its meaning), the table ownership per SDK, the domain events and the fact that emission is best-effort so a 2xx does not prove an event landed, and exactly what an application may and may not extend. AC4: .github/workflows/neutrality-gate.yml runs on pull_request filtered to packages/**, and also on push to main so a direct push cannot bypass it. QA edge cases: comments are deliberately NOT scanned — a comment saying 'holds no patient-specific logic' is the author documenting neutrality, and flagging it would teach people to delete the explanation rather than the coupling; tests are not scanned because fixtures need concrete data to be readable; apps/** is out of scope because a vertical application is supposed to know its own domain; the gate is dependency-free and the workflow has no install step, since a gate that breaks on unrelated dependency issues gets disabled. PRECEDENT: on its first run the gate found real pre-existing coupling — sdk-parsing had patient_name, medication and prescription hardcoded as classifier and extractor defaults. Rather than allowlist them, the vocabulary moved to document-vocabulary.json as replaceable data, leaving the TypeScript holding only the mechanism; behaviour was unchanged and all 40 sdk-parsing tests stayed green.

errorCases.name: A vertical literal in SDK source fails the build
errorCases.message: NEUTRALITY GATE FAILED — <n> vertical-specific literal(s) in SDK source.
errorCases.when: a vertical noun, stage name, role branch or hardcoded business rule appears in the source of a platform package; the build fails and the offending file:line is named so the author can act

errorCases.name: Suppressing rather than fixing is the wrong response
errorCases.message: Move the concept behind a caller-supplied resolver, a config value, or a tenant-configurable rule
errorCases.when: an author is tempted to allowlist a literal instead of removing the coupling; the contract records the sdk-parsing precedent showing the correct fix is to push the domain out to configuration, which preserved behaviour and kept every test green
